primaryTasks: Look up an incident by id, title or location and read its current status, assignee and assessment state
Arrive by deep link from My Work / Assessments / Mission Center / Event Group and jump onward to the Event Group, map, assessment or submission
(Reporters) check whether a filed field report is still awaiting intake or has been accepted into the record

painPoints.issue: The 'record view' never shows the record: description, first_observed_at, first_occurred_at, current_stage, office_code, incident_key, reporter, created_at, resolved_at and resolution_comment exist on Incident but only six columns render; deep links labelled 'Open incident record' land on a highlighted table row with less information than the page they came from
'Event Group #id' link sends maintenance-only reporters to a RoleRoute-gated page that bounces them to /submissions, a page with no nav entry for their role
'No assessment' is shown to non-operational users even when an assessment exists, because assessments are only fetched for operational roles
'Loading classification…' is a permanent state whenever the backend returns no classification row (items and classifications are set together)
Count 'X of Y incidents' mixes the per-tab filtered count with the total across both tabs
Pressing Refresh while on /incidents/:id forcibly switches the tab back to the target's tab because the highlight effect depends on items
Deep link to an unknown id, or to an id hidden by the status/unclaimed filter, gives no feedback at all
Vocabulary drift on one screen: 'Unclaimed only' filter vs 'Unassigned' column; 'Awaiting intake' tab vs 'review' in the banner vs 'triage' in My Work
NEW status uses the --bad red token, so the intake tab is a wall of red badges signalling error rather than newness
Accessibility: tab switcher is two buttons without role=tablist/aria-selected; search input and status select have no accessible label beyond placeholder; links are colour-only
Whole-list fetch (limit=1000) plus classification and assessment fetches on every visit/refresh, filtered client-side; no pagination, silent truncation past 1000
One busy flag and one error slot serve list loading, form validation and creation: Refresh disables the create panel, and a form validation message appears in the page banner below the panel
Intake banner tells reporters to use My Work, and My Work tells reporters to use Incidents - a circular pointer for the role that files reports

strengths: Clear conceptual split between accepted records and awaiting-intake reports, documented in code and echoed in tab labels and banners (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:46-52,222-223,261-269)
Deep link /incidents/:id auto-selects the right tab, scrolls and highlights the row (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:102-112,298)
Instant client-side search across id, title, description, district, county, route and post mile (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:116-130)
Consistent CSS-variable theming (--brand/--good/--bad/--panel with color-mix) so the page works in light, dark and coastal themes (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:262-272; incidentUiModel.ts:63-71)
Each row is a hub with links to Event Group, map, assessment and submissions (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:304,309,315,318)
Tab counts double as an intake backlog indicator (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:114,222-223)
Caltrans location vocabulary (D/County/R/PM) via a shared formatter (features/eventGroups/eventGroupTypes.ts:71-79)

breakpointsUsed: Header flex-wrap so Cancel drops under the title on narrow widths (46)
phoneRisks: Single column of 10 fields plus the files block is roughly 2.5 screens tall; the Create button sits at the bottom and validation errors render in the page banner below the panel, so the reason for a failed submit is often off-screen (IncidentCreatePanel.tsx:67-185; IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:271)

No geolocation or map pick: a field worker on a phone types six-decimal latitude/longitude by hand; California longitudes are negative and type=number keypads often hide the minus key (IncidentCreatePanel.tsx:83-104)
datetime-local twice on a phone is fine natively, but there is no 'now' shortcut for First observed (76-78)
Native file input with no capture attribute means no direct camera shortcut; no thumbnails for chosen photos (131-138)
'Remove' buttons are ~26px tall, below the 44px touch minimum (157)
Three dismiss controls (header Cancel, footer Cancel, toolbar Close report) and no confirm-discard, so a stray tap loses a half-typed report (53-60,169-176; IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:239)
tabletRisks: md 2-column grid pairs Title with Description; the min-h-20 textarea makes row one uneven and pushes the required First observed field below the fold on 768px landscape (67-78)
datetime-local inputs are wide on iPadOS and can exceed a 2-column cell at 768px because inputClass sets no width constraints (18,76-81)
desktopNotes: xl 3-column layout leaves a blank spacer cell in row two and splits location fields across rows three (Lat | Lon | District) and four (County | Route | Post mile) (67-126)
No autoFocus on Title when the panel opens; not wrapped in <form> so Enter does nothing (44,69)

painPoints.issue: Coordinates must be hand-typed; no 'use my location' (navigator.geolocation) and no map picker even though Mission Center already hosts an ArcGIS map
Validation is imperative and page-level: no required/aria-invalid attributes, no field-level messages, errors surface in the shared page banner outside the panel
Attachment failures cannot be retried: the incident is created, the panel resets, the notice truncates to two failures, and this page has no attachments UI to add the files afterwards
Dead incident_type field in the form model, never rendered or sent
Duplicate Cancel buttons and duplicated 'unclassified' copy inside one panel
Raw attachment kind enum shown to users; SKETCH is inferred only when a PNG's file name contains 'sketch'
formatCoordinate on blur silently wipes a non-numeric entry to an empty string
Shared busy flag: while the list refreshes the whole form is disabled, and while creating the Refresh button is disabled
'Supporting files' label is a bare <label> with no htmlFor, so the file input has no accessible name
No route for intake (e.g. /incidents/new), so the primary mobile task for field workers cannot be deep-linked or bookmarked

strengths: Every field is an implicit <label> wrapper, giving accessible names for free (IncidentCreatePanel.tsx:20-28)
Blur normalisation of route, post mile and coordinates enforces ERIS precision rules at entry (IncidentCreatePanel.tsx:91,102,116,124; utils/precision.ts)
Attachment kind is inferred client-side so the user does not pick a type per file (incidentUiModel.ts:38-48)
Success path reloads, switches to the intake tab and tells the reporter what happens next (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:189-198)
Honest 'unclassified until field assessment' messaging matches the real workflow (IncidentCreatePanel.tsx:49-51)
inputMode=decimal and step=0.000001 on coordinate inputs give a numeric keypad and sane precision (IncidentCreatePanel.tsx:85-87)

painPoints.evidence: components/WorkflowTree.tsx:77,110 and api/workflowTree.ts:71 have no importers; IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx never references them

painPoints.issue: Hard-coded Tailwind palette tuned for a dark background (text-emerald-300, text-sky-200, text-amber-200, text-red-200/300, bg-slate-500/600, text-black on dots) breaks contrast on the Light and Coastal themes the shell offers; every other panel in this area uses --good/--bad/--brand tokens
Raw codes leak into the UI: assessment state and event_type are rendered unlabelled although a shared assessmentStateLabel helper exists
Unicode glyph icons (⮌ U+2B8C, ►, ■, ○) are font-dependent and not aria-hidden, so screen readers announce them before the status label
Every node card is a focusable <button> even when it has no details to reveal
Linked incident/location ids are plain text rather than links to /incidents/:id
disposition is typed but never rendered

strengths: ModalDialog supplies focus trap, Escape, backdrop close, focus restore and role=dialog/aria-modal/aria-labelledby (ui/ModalDialog.tsx:43-126)
Workflow status and path codes are mapped to plain-English labels in one place (WorkflowTree.tsx:11-28)
Current-owner card ring is a clear 'you are here' cue (WorkflowTree.tsx:49,101)
Progressive disclosure of notes/email via a Details toggle with aria-expanded (WorkflowTree.tsx:47-59)
Orientation-aware connectors (↓ stacked, → horizontal) show the design already considered narrow layouts (WorkflowTree.tsx:73-75)

crossCutting: Dead and legacy code: components/WorkflowTree.tsx and api/workflowTree.ts are never imported; pages/ProjectDetailPage.tsx is unrouted (App.tsx:77-78 redirects /projects/* to /event-groups) yet still carries an 'Open in Incidents' button (ProjectDetailPage.tsx:125); features/projects/ProjectAssociationDialog.tsx (lines 52-102) duplicates features/eventGroups/EventGroupAssociationDialog.tsx (lines 84-140) against parallel /incidents/:id/*-context, nearby-* and *-association endpoints; IncidentCreateForm.incident_type is a dead field (incidentUiModel.ts:5,19).

Vocabulary drift for the same object and state across this area and its neighbours: 'report' (Close report, 'Incident reported', 'field report'), 'incident', 'Create incident'; 'intake' (tab) vs 'review' (banner) vs 'triage' (My Work TriageWorkItem, WorkflowTree PATH_LABEL 'Awaiting triage'); 'Unclaimed' (filter) vs 'Unassigned' (column, WorkflowTree); tab 'Awaiting intake' vs stage code COORDINATOR_REVIEW.

Four overlapping state vocabularies can appear in a single table row: incident status (NEW/IN_PROGRESS/RESOLVED badge), current_stage (drives tabs but is never displayed), classification_status text, and assessment state badge - each with its own colour mapping (incidentUiModel.ts:63-71; incidentClassification.ts:26-31; features/assessments/AssessmentDetailPanel.tsx:71-77; WorkflowTree.tsx:11-20).

No shared Button/Badge/Input primitives: primary, secondary and small buttons are repeated as literal class strings with slightly different padding and radius (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:211,239,243; IncidentCreatePanel.tsx:57,157,173,181; WorkflowTree.tsx:132), and three separate pill implementations exist (IncidentStatusBadge, AssessmentStateBadge mini, WorkflowTree STATUS pills).

Theme-token discipline is inconsistent: incidents pages use --brand/--good/--bad color-mix tokens, while WorkflowTree uses raw Tailwind palette classes plus fixed rgba shadows (WorkflowTree.tsx:12-19,49) and AppShell also hard-codes rgba(31,94,255,0.25) for the active nav item (ui/AppShell.tsx:41).

Links are colour-only everywhere ('text-[var(--brand)] hover:underline'), which fails non-colour link identification on touch devices and for colour-blind users (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:263,267,304,309,315,318).

Accessibility gaps: tab switcher without tablist/aria-selected; search input and status select rely on placeholder/no label; file input label not associated; unicode status glyphs not aria-hidden; raw role codes in the header (AppShell.tsx:157); several controls under the 44px touch minimum (Remove, Close, native checkbox).

Mobile shell: below lg (1024px) the entire navigation renders inline above page content with no drawer or hamburger (ui/AppShell.tsx:164), so phones and portrait tablets scroll past the nav on every visit - the users most likely on a phone are the field workers this area's intake panel serves.

Role-gating asymmetry: /incidents is open to every role, but row links go to RoleRoute-gated pages (/event-groups, /assessments) that bounce non-operational users to /submissions (auth/RoleRoute.tsx:19), a page with no nav entry for them; My Work and Incidents point reporters at each other (MyWorkPage.tsx:112; IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:263).

Data-loading pattern: three whole-table fetches on every visit and Refresh (incidents limit=1000, classifications for every id, assessments limit=1000) with client-side filtering and no pagination (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:79-86).

Feedback pattern: single page-level error and notice slots are shared by list loading, form validation and upload results, so messages appear far from their cause (IncidentsOperationsPage.tsx:68-70,163-167,271-272).

The 'record view' has no detail surface: the Incident type carries description, timestamps, stage, office, key, reporter and resolution fields (api/types.ts:243-277) that no screen in this area renders, and the unmounted WorkflowTree is the only component that would have shown per-step history.
